analysis.notes: The textbook ii–V–I tune. Every phrase is either a major ii–V–I in Bb (Cm7–F7–Bbmaj7) or a minor ii–V–i in G minor (Am7b5–D7–Gm6), and the two keys are relatives, so one scale (Bb major / G natural minor) covers almost everything. The exception is the D7: raise the F to F# (harmonic minor) over it. The last eight bars add a short chain of ii–Vs (Gm7–C7, Fm7–Bb7) that walks down to Ebmaj7.

learning.why: The classic first standard for a reason: it teaches the major and minor ii–V–I side by side, in relative keys, at a medium swing tempo. If you can play Autumn Leaves convincingly you can play the language.
concepts: Harmonic minor over V7 in minor
drills: Loop bars 1–4 (Cm7–F7–Bbmaj7–Ebmaj7) and comp with shells until the 3rds and 7ths move by step.
Loop bars 5–8 (Am7b5–D7–Gm6) and practise the F# on the D7 in your lines.
Play the whole form with only the 3rd and 7th of each chord as a two-note solo.
Use the ii–V–I gym in Bb and Gm at 140 BPM.
milestones: Know the form and changes from memory
Comp shells through the form without looking
Comp drop-2 voicings with the trio
Play a chord-tone solo over the whole form
Play the melody from memory (learn it by ear from a recording)
